<issue_description>
spanner-client: Retry PDML on "Received unexpected EOS on DATA frame from server" 
This bug is related to the Spanner client library.

For long lived transactions (>= 30 minutes), in the case of large PDML changes, it is possible that the gRPC connection is terminated with an error "Received unexpected EOS on DATA frame from server".

In this case, we need to retry the transaction either with the received resume token obtained on reading the stream or from scratch. This will ensure that the PDML transaction continues to execute until it is successful or a hard timeout is reached.

We have already implemented such change in the Java client library, for more information see this PR: https://github.com/googleapis/java-spanner/pull/360.

In order to test the fix, we can use a large spanner database. Please speak to @thiagotnunes for more details.

   135	        unix_timestamp=1335020400,
   136	    )
   137	
   138	
   139	Select records using a Transaction
   140	~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
   141	
   142	Once you have a transaction object (such as the first argument sent to
   143	``run_in_transaction``), reading data is easy:
   144	
   145	.. code:: python
   146	
   147	    # Define a SELECT query.
   148	    query = """SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, p.telephone
   149	        FROM employees as e, phones as p
   150	        WHERE p.employee_id == e.employee_id"""
   151	
   152	    # Execute the query and return results.
   153	    result = transaction.execute_sql(query)
   154	    for row in result.rows:
   155	        print(row)
   156	
   157	
   158	Insert records using Data Manipulation Language (DML) with a Transaction
   159	~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
   160	
   161	Use the ``execute_update()`` method to execute a DML statement:
   162	
   163	.. code:: python
   164	
   165	    spanner_client = spanner.Client()
   166	    instance = spanner_client.instance(instance_id)
   167	    database = instance.database(database_id)
   168	
   169	    def insert_singers(transaction):
   170	        row_ct = transaction.execute_update(
   171	            "INSERT Singers (SingerId, FirstName, LastName) "
   172	            " VALUES (10, 'Virginia', 'Watson')"
   173	        )
   174	
   175	        print("{} record(s) inserted.".format(row_ct))
   176	
   177	    database.run_in_transaction(insert_singers)
   178	
   179	
   180	Insert records using Mutations with a Transaction
   181	~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
   182	
   183	To add one or more records to a table, use ``insert``:
   184	
   185	.. code:: python
   186	
   187	    transaction.insert(
   188	        'citizens',
   189	        columns=['email', 'first_name', 'last_name', 'age'],
   190	        values=[
   191	            ['phred@exammple.com', 'Phred', 'Phlyntstone', 32],
   192	            ['bharney@example.com', 'Bharney', 'Rhubble', 31],
   193	        ],
   194	    )
   195	
   196	
   197	Update records using Data Manipulation Language (DML) with a Transaction
   198	~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
   199	
   200	.. code:: python
   201	
   202	    spanner_client = spanner.Client()
   203	    instance = spanner_client.instance(instance_id)
   204	    database = instance.database(database_id)
   205	
   206	    def update_albums(transaction):
   207	        row_ct = transaction.execute_update(
   208	            "UPDATE Albums "
   209	            "SET MarketingBudget = MarketingBudget * 2 "
   210	            "WHERE SingerId = 1 and AlbumId = 1"
   211	        )
   212	
   213	        print("{} record(s) updated.".format(row_ct))
   214	
   215	    database.run_in_transaction(update_albums)
   216	
   217	
   218	Update records using Mutations with a Transaction
   219	~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
   220	
   221	``Transaction.update`` updates one or more existing records in a table.  Fails
   222	if any of the records does not already exist.
   223	
   224	.. code:: python
   225	
   226	    transaction.update(
   227	        'citizens',
   228	        columns=['email', 'age'],
   229	        values=[
   230	            ['phred@exammple.com', 33],
   231	            ['bharney@example.com', 32],
   232	        ],
   233	    )
